security_audit.summary: The static Ruby or shell backtick findings are false positives from Markdown fences and inline .NET identifiers. The Azure environment variable entries are placeholders, not evidence of secret access or exfiltration. One real semantic issue remains: the skill demonstrates printing Cosmos DB keys and connection strings to console.

remediation.issue: The sample prints Cosmos DB account keys and connection strings.
remediation.suggestion: Remove console logging of keys and connection strings. Show retrieval only when needed, and tell users to redact or store secrets securely.

remediation.issue: The service principal secret placeholder lacks handling guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend managed identity, secret stores, and local environment files excluded from version control for AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET.

remediation.issue: Package installation commands are shown without verification guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify package versions and review project changes before running installation commands.

content.user_title: Manage Cosmos DB with Azure ARM for .NET
content.value_statement: Provisioning Cosmos DB with the management SDK requires the right Azure ARM resource hierarchy. This skill shows how to create accounts, databases, containers, throughput settings, and authentication flows in .NET.
actual_capabilities: Shows NuGet packages for Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB and Azure.Identity.
Explains when to use the management plane SDK instead of the data plane SDK.
Provides C# examples for Cosmos DB accounts, SQL databases, and SQL containers.
Demonstrates manual and autoscale throughput configuration.
Shows ARM error handling with RequestFailedException.
Lists key Cosmos DB resource types and related reference topics.
limitations: Covers management plane tasks, not document CRUD or query operations.
Requires an Azure subscription, resource group, permissions, and configured credentials.
Does not cover private endpoints, backup policy, governance, or compliance controls.
Package versions may change and should be verified before use.

use_cases.title: Provision Cosmos DB Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Create accounts, databases, containers, and throughput settings through the Azure Resource Manager SDK.

use_cases.title: Standardize .NET Management Code
use_cases.description: Use consistent resource hierarchy patterns, authentication, and ARM operation handling across platform tooling.

use_cases.title: Choose the Correct Azure SDK
use_cases.description: Separate management plane workflows from data plane document access in a .NET application plan.

prompt_templates.title: Identify SDK Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain when I should use Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB instead of Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos for a .NET project.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Account Creation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a .NET workflow to create a Cosmos DB SQL API account in an existing Azure resource group.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Containers and Throughput
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Cosmos DB SQL database and container setup with partition key choices, indexing, and autoscale throughput.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Provisioning
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Cosmos DB ARM management approach for authentication, long running operations, error handling, and secret exposure risks.

output_examples.input: Create a SQL API account and first container in East US.
output: Resource hierarchy from subscription to resource group to account.
Account, database, container, and throughput steps in execution order.
Notes for permissions, naming, and long running operation handling.

output_examples.input: Compare manual and autoscale throughput for a new database.
output_examples.output: The skill can summarize when fixed throughput is simpler, when autoscale fits variable traffic, and what values must be configured.

output_examples.input: Review a Cosmos DB management snippet for safe logging.
output_examples.output: The skill can identify key and connection string exposure, suggest redaction, and recommend safer credential handling.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential with least privilege Azure roles.
Redact keys, connection strings, subscription identifiers, and error details before sharing output.
Validate region, account name, partition key, and throughput choices before applying changes.
anti_patterns: Printing primary keys or connection strings to logs or terminal output.
Using the management SDK for document CRUD, queries, or stored procedure execution.
Hardcoding service principal secrets, subscription IDs, or account keys in source files.

faq.question: Does this skill manage Cosmos DB data records?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Azure Resource Manager tasks, such as accounts, databases, containers, and throughput.

faq.question: Which .NET package does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB with Azure.Identity for authentication.

faq.question: Can it help choose between management and data plane SDKs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use management operations and when to use Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos for data access.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Real use requires Azure credentials with permissions for the target subscription and resource group.

faq.question: Can it generate production ready infrastructure code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation, but production designs still need security, networking, and compliance review.

faq.question: What should users avoid when using it?
faq.answer: Users should avoid logging keys, committing secrets, or running management changes without reviewing their Azure impact.
